findings.rationale: SC's uploaded updates are normal in rounds 1-10 (cos with the median update 0.99 down to 0.35, norm ratio about 0.7-1.1). From round 11 onward the update norm jumps to about 2.2-2.8x the median and the cosine turns negative (-0.07 at round 11, falling to about -0.5 by round 18), a persistent, systematic reversal rather than random scatter. The abrupt onset and the scaled, direction-reversed pattern fit a manipulated (sign-flipped/scaled) upload. Local evidence is only weakly anomalous: the round-20 CITL is -0.056 (z=-4.0) and subgroup O/E is elevated, but AUC is normal (0.823), so this is a lead rather than a clean confirmation. Confidence is moderate.

WI's updates are normal through round 10 (cos 0.97 to 0.74, norm ratio about 1.0-1.4). From round 11 the norm roughly doubles (1.77 to 2.3x the median) and the cosine turns negative (about -0.00 at round 11, -0.31 by round 14, -0.44 by round 17), with the same onset round as SC. The local model looks normal (AUC 0.820, CITL -0.028, not flagged), and the update pattern is the main evidence, so this is moderate confidence. A small feature shift after round 11 is also visible in drift_by_round, but it is not clearly beyond noise.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views (updates, performance, drift, feature tails, subgroup outcomes for Sex, AgeGroup and Income), then confirmed leads with narrower queries. Two clients, SC and WI, show the same clear break at round 11: the update norm roughly doubles or more and the cosine to the median update turns negative and persists through round 20, while their rounds 1-10 updates looked normal. I report both as poisoning from round 11, with moderate confidence. The fault type is inferred from the update anomaly, since local AUC is normal for both; SC's CITL and subgroup O/E deviations are only moderate (z about 4) and are not treated as separate findings. Other leads were judged to be small-sample noise and not reported: GU (small n=708, erratic per-round updates with no consistent free-rider pattern), and the scattered feature-tail and subgroup outliers, which are at |z_noise| of about 3-5 across many clients and do not form a consistent pattern. Budget spent: 19 of 20 epsilon, with 0 remaining.
